Or add the file to the shell checks' `exclude:` pattern in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, when the file is not real bash. Before this change, a pre-commit run named the broken line only.
- README `rev:` pins now name `v1.0.0`, the tag that actually exists — the
  documented `v0.2.0` never shipped, so every copy-pasted consumer config failed
  at `pre-commit install-hooks` with an unresolvable rev.
- The pip package version is no longer a stale hand-maintained copy: `pyproject.toml`
  declares `version` as dynamic and reads it from `package.json`, the one file the
  release pipeline bumps, so `pip install ci-truth-serum` reports the released
  version instead of a frozen `0.2.0`.
- `check-versionless-install`: an interpreter name appearing inside the hint text
  being excused no longer counts as executing it. `missing_gate "install it with
'bash setup.bash' (or 'uv tool install pre-commit')"` was flagged because
  `bash` occurred somewhere in the line; the executor is now matched at the
  command word (through `sudo`, `env VAR=…` and an absolute path), so
  `bash -c "pip install x"` still fires and a message that merely names an
  interpreter does not.
- `check-versionless-install`: an install inside a quoted string is only flagged
  when something executes that string (`bash -c`, `sh -c`, `eval`, `ssh`,
  `xargs`). Help text and log messages that name an install for a human —
  `gb_error "install it: apt install coreutils"`,
  `require_command jq "e.g. apt-get install jq"` — no longer fire, without this
  lint having to know every project's logger names. A `;`/`&&` inside a quoted
  string no longer starts a new command either, while an install after a real
  separator (`note "x" && apt-get install -y curl`) still fires.
- `check-versionless-install`: a redirection in the argument list (`>&2`, `2>&1`,
  `>log`) is no longer read as an unpinned package name, which flagged
  `apt-get install --only-upgrade -y "$pin_spec" >&2` even though its only real
  spec was pinned.
- The annotation window again accepts the line directly above a construct when that line also carries code. Consolidating the window onto one definition narrowed it by accident: the block above was walked through comment-only lines, so a reason written as a trailing comment on the line that opens the construct — `if  # pin-exempt: <reason>` above a `curl` — stopped counting, and the check fired at an annotation that was already there. The window is now the construct's span, the line directly above it whatever that line holds, and the unbroken comment block above that.
- `check-workflow-pipefail` and `check-inline-run-length` now emit GitHub `::error file=…,line=…::` annotations pointing at the offending step, instead of a bare `::error::` with the path buried in free text. Their violations are now clickable in the GitHub UI and the file-changed view, matching every other workflow lint.
- Hooks that hand-parse workflow YAML now close several fail-opens: `check-always-reporter` and `check-required-reporter` also check list-form `on: [pull_request, …]` (previously only mapping-form `on:` was inspected, so a gated required-check workflow missing its `always()` reporter slipped through); `check-concurrency` now flags a **job-level** `concurrency:` block that omits `cancel-in-progress`, not just the workflow-level one; `check-claude-model` anchors each violation to its real step via the parsed source line instead of a positional grep that a commented-out `uses:` line could misalign; and all eight of these lints report a workflow they can't parse as YAML as a violation instead of crashing with a traceback. The `cancel-in-progress-not-required`, `static-concurrency-ok`, and `concurrency-not-required` opt-outs are now honored only on a real `#` comment line, not anywhere in the file's bytes.
- `check-workflow-pipefail`, `check-inline-run-length`, and `check-externalized-markers` now report a workflow file they can't parse as YAML as a violation, instead of silently treating it as clean. A malformed workflow used to read as "no findings" — a false-green on the exact file the lint exists to verify; YAML syntax is still actionlint's job, but a document PyYAML can't even build is no longer waved through.

### Security

- Every opt-out annotation now requires its token to stand ALONE, on both ends.
  The shared matcher delimited the token with `\b`, which matches at a word/`-`
  transition — and nearly every token in this package is hyphenated. So one
  hook's opt-out was satisfiable by a DIFFERENT annotation whose slug merely
  contained it: `# really-allow-unbounded: …` suppressed a hook asking for
  `allow-unbounded`, and (in the reason-free form) `# pin-comment-ok-ish`
  suppressed one asking for `pin-comment-ok`. A neighbouring lint's marker could
  silently disarm another lint — a fail-open. Both edges are now stated as
  zero-width lookarounds over the characters a token is spelled from.
- `opted_out` (the concurrency lints' whole-file comment scan) was a bare
  substring test, open at both ends: `# no-static-concurrency-ok-here` — or prose
  merely mentioning the token — suppressed the check. It now routes through the
  same shared matcher, so it inherits the stand-alone-token guarantee.
- `check-frozen-head-sha`'s `# frozen-head-ok:` opt-out no longer accepts a
  reason borrowed from the NEXT line. It hand-spelled the reason gap as `\s*`,
  which crosses a newline, and it searches a whole multi-line job block — so a
  bare `# frozen-head-ok:` ending a line suppressed the lint with an empty claim.
- `check-pinned-downloads` and `check-pipefail-grep-pipe` no longer accept an opt-out or verification token that lives in a comment or a bare substring, closing two supply-chain lint bypasses. `check-pinned-downloads` now classifies comment vs. code with the bash grammar (`tree-sitter-bash`) before scanning, so a verification token mentioned only in a comment (`# TODO: verify with sha256sum`) no longer satisfies the gate — the `sha256sum`/`cosign`/`gpg` check must sit in executed code. Both lints now route their `# pin-exempt:` / `# pipefail-grep-ok:` opt-outs through one shared comment-scoped matcher that requires the token inside a real `#` comment with a stated reason, so a token smuggled into a URL path or string (`curl -o x https://cdn/pin-exempt/x | sh`) can no longer silence the check.
- `release-prep.yaml`: the version-bump job read its bootstrap script (`.github/scripts/release-prep-bump-version.sh`) out of the pull request's own checkout, so a PR that rewrote that file executed with `TEMPLATE_SYNC_TOKEN_ORG` and the model credentials in its environment — the staging that script performs never applied to the script itself. The job now stages the bootstrap from the base ref and runs that copy. Found by dogfooding the new `check-untrusted-exec` hook.
- The three Claude reviewer steps now grant `Read`/`Edit` with paths instead of
  bare whole-tool names. A bare `Read` or `Write` is applied after the per-path
  check and overrides it, so the `--add-dir` beside it confined nothing: the
  reviewer could read any path on the runner (including the artifact token) and
  overwrite any file in the checkout. Each step now reads the workspace and the
  sanitized input directory, and writes only its own output file.
- The phone-home secret scan verifies the gitleaks download against a pinned
  checksum again, instead of piping an unverified release tarball into `tar`.
- `check-trusted-base` now also reports a privileged `pull_request(_target)` job
  that checks out an author-chosen **BASE** ref (`github.event.pull_request.base.ref`
  / `.sha`, `github.base_ref`), not only the PR head. A PR's base is a branch the
  author picks: push branch `A` carrying a rewritten build/release script, open PR
  `B` _based on_ `A`, and a job that stages "the base branch" stages and executes
  `A` with the org credentials live — while PR `B`'s own diff stays clean, so a
  "does this PR edit the machinery?" refusal never sees it. Narrowing the base to
  `main || master` is not a fix: on a repo whose default branch is `main`,
  `master` is an ordinary pushable branch name. Re-derive the default branch from
  `$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH` and refuse on every negative path instead. Scoped to a base
  ref passed to `actions/checkout` — a base context used as _data_ (a diff range,
  a version baseline) never materializes a tree and is not reported. Head-ref
  findings are unchanged, message included.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-07-19

### Added

- Initial release: fast, offline pre-commit lints that catch CI honesty lies
  (exit codes masked by pipes, required checks that never report) and
  supply-chain identity lies (mutable image tags, unpinned downloads) before a
  green check can hide them, together with the changelog-fragment workflow and
  the tag/release automation that ship them.
